A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TRACE study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and the movement of case studies from Appendix D to Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original meta-evaluation experiments on Meta-GTA and Meta-m&m’s, comparisons with LLM-as-a-Judge and PIPA, and evaluations of nine tool-augmented agents on GTA.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Magentic-One evaluation on GAIA, failed-trajectory efficiency results, and a human-validation agreement result.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix D.1 introduce a multi-agent adaptation: separate evidence banks for individual agents and access to the combined banks when assessing orchestrator hallucinations. The underlying TRACE metrics and existing evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds actual evaluation on GAIA’s general-assistant tasks using Magentic-One, extending coverage to multi-agent trajectories beyond the retained GTA and m&m’s task sets. GAIA was only discussed as related work in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated competing approaches remain LLM-as-a-Judge and PIPA, with unchanged membership in Tables 1–3. Magentic-One is an additional system evaluated using TRACE, not a competing trajectory-evaluation method.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds efficiency evaluation conditioned on failed GTA trajectories alongside the retained success-only main evaluation. The GAIA experiment evaluates Magentic-One with four existing evaluator models. Previously stated settings, including temperature 0, 4096 maximum tokens, and ten action turns, are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 compares failed and successful trajectories to investigate survivorship bias and the relationship between efficiency and task success. The evidence-bank comparison, multiple-trajectory robustness analysis, token-consumption analysis, and existing case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same standard deviations across alternative trajectories. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The newly reported human agreement percentage is a validation outcome rather than a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds two substantive result sets: Magentic-One/GAIA scores in Table 7, including 20.45 accuracy and efficiency scores of 88.06–97.07, and failed GTA trajectory scores in Table 8. Appendix B.1 additionally reports 98.79% human-validation agreement. Original Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–4 retain their results; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The trajectory and evidence-bank definitions, efficiency and hallucination formulas, and meta-evaluation accuracy equations are unchanged. The added optimality discussion and suggestion to combine accuracy with efficiency do not introduce a formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: reference-free trajectory assessment through an evidence bank, evaluation across three dimensions, and diagnostic insights beyond answer accuracy. The shortened abstract does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies efficiency as detecting unnecessary evidence within the observed trajectory rather than guaranteeing a globally optimal path, and clarifies that unsupported internal knowledge counts as hallucination. Appendix D adds discussion of survivorship bias, suggests combining accuracy and efficiency, and interprets the GAIA results as evidence of broader applicability.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement removes v1’s explicit statement that all GTA baseline results are supplied in supplementary materials. The code link, meta-dataset availability statement, model versions, hyperparameters, and prompts remain. This establishes reduced access documentation, not actual withdrawal of the supplementary results.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fourney et al.’s Magentic-One and Li et al.’s ReSeek to support the multi-agent extension and hallucination convention. Most other citation changes update publication metadata for existing works, including the Nelson-to-Das attribution for the same Needle in the Haystack paper.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, explanatory paragraphs are inserted, and a new Further Analysis appendix precedes the relocated case studies. The ethics statement becomes a generic impact statement, acknowledgements are added, and author/header information changes. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Tables 7–8 are added, and the two final prompt figures are separated onto individual pages. Existing illustrations and prompt contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope clarification and adds multi-agent and failure-conditioned evidence absent from v1. However, the new evidence introduces unresolved reporting problems: several Table 8 averages disagree with their listed scores, and Mistral’s successful-trajectory efficiency becomes 0 despite being undefined in Table 4. Section 5.1 also promises GAIA adaptivity results that Table 7 does not report. These benefits and reliability problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
